overview: The Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport is a gunship / fighter whose design philosophy reflects the industrial and strategic priorities of Clone Wars through Mandalorian Era. Kom'rk-class ships serve Mandalorian super commandos as troop transports and heavy gun platforms. Production estimates place the class at ~200 units, though wartime losses, capture, and black-market duplication make precise fleet registries unreliable.
history:
Engineering teams first finalized the Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport blueprints during the political climate of Clone Wars through Mandalorian Era. The gunship / fighter was intended to solve specific fleet gaps—whether planetary assault, convoy escort, starfighter superiority, or terror bombardment—and shipwrights iterated hull plates, reactor output, and crew compartments accordingly.

Once deployed, the Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport appeared in fleet actions that defined its reputation. Kom'rk-class ships serve Mandalorian super commandos as troop transports and heavy gun platforms. Combat logs show crews exploiting the class's strengths while improvising fixes for known weaknesses under fire, a pattern repeated across every major galactic conflict.

As doctrine evolved, rival factions studied captured Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport hulls. Refit yards duplicated weapons mounts and sensor suites; some variants never appeared in official manifests. Estimated production of ~200 units therefore understates how many similar silhouettes operated under alternate insignia.

Surviving Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport vessels now sit in museum orbits, mercenary fleets, and scrap worlds. Historians treat the class as a measure of how galactic wars industrialize violence—each hull a factory product that outlived the politicians who ordered it.
significance:
The Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport demonstrates how gunship / fighter design shapes campaign outcomes. Its layout influenced successor programs and remains a case study in naval academies.

With roughly ~200 units hulls associated with Clone Wars through Mandalorian Era, the class became a visual symbol of its faction's reach—recognizable in holonet footage and feared in convoy manifests.

Engineers still debate whether the Kom'rk-class Fighter/Transport prioritized firepower over crew survival; that trade-off defines its legacy in both propaganda and honest after-action reports.
